narrative:
Based on the information provided, the model predicts that you have a 22% chance of not passing your final year. Because this probability is above the school’s threshold of 10%, you are required to take additional remedial courses to support your success.

The prediction was influenced most strongly by three aspects of your background and choices. First, your record shows that you have not failed any classes before, which is a positive sign and actually helped lower your risk compared to others. This means your past academic performance is on par with students who typically do not need remedial support.

However, the model also considered your mother’s education level, which is listed as primary school. Among students who do not need remedial courses, only a small percentage have mothers with this level of education, while most have mothers with secondary or higher education. This factor increased your predicted risk, as students with less parental educational support sometimes face more challenges in school.

Lastly, your main reason for choosing this school was its proximity to home. While this is a common choice, students who select their school based on academic programs or reputation tend to have slightly better outcomes. This factor helped reduce your risk somewhat, but not enough to offset the influence of the other factors.

Given these influences, taking remedial courses is a precaution to help you stay on track. Use this opportunity to strengthen your skills and seek support where needed, so you can confidently progress toward graduation.
